BUG: Time Clock user CAN read organization Settings via API (should be blocked)
current_excerpt: EXPECTED: the request should return 403 Forbidden because the Time Clock role has no Settings access. ACTUAL (2026-07-13, staging): the request returns 200 OK ... a permission LEAK. Linked to the Jira bug: "BE — Time Clock Role Permissions Not Properly Enforced".

proposed_text.title: Time Clock user reading organization Settings via API returns 200 (backend does not enforce — expected)
proposed_text.custom_expected:
The request returns 200 OK with the organization's work-order settings.

This is the expected, accepted behaviour: the Product Owner confirmed (SV-7958, 2026-07-14) that the backend only enforces permissions on some endpoints and intentionally leaves others open by design. This read endpoint is not gated on the backend; the Settings area is instead hidden from the Time Clock user in the app (front-end), which is considered sufficient.

reason: SV-7958 closed Done with the PO ruling that this observed behaviour is expected (backend enforcement not required; front-end hides the surface) — the case asserted a 403 the build will never return, a prime nightly-automation false failure.
citation: SV-7958 Sasha Grosman 2026-07-14 ("What was reported observed ... is expected. We only block BE permission when appropriate"); ticket closed Done.

title: BUG: Time Clock user CAN create a Customer via API (should be blocked)
current_excerpt: EXPECTED: the request should return 403 Forbidden ... ACTUAL (2026-07-13, staging): the request returns 201 Created and a real customer is created — a serious permission LEAK (the create endpoint is missing the gate that the view and delete endpoints have).

proposed_text.title: Time Clock user creating a Customer via API returns 201 (backend does not enforce — accepted by PO)
proposed_text.custom_expected:
The request returns 201 Created and a customer record is created.

Per the Product Owner (SV-7958, 2026-07-14) the backend permission gaps observed on this role are expected/accepted for now — the backend does not gate this create endpoint and the front end does not expose customer creation to the Time Clock user. NOTE for QA: this is a WRITE/create leak (not merely a read); it was explicitly reported as "Critical" and the PO still accepted it and closed SV-7958 Done. Flag to the PO if a backend gate is later desired, but the current expected result is 201.

reason: SV-7958 was closed Done after Bilal explicitly reported the POST /api/customers/create 201 leak as Critical; the PO ruled the observed behaviour expected. Case must assert the accepted 201, with a QA note that this is a write-leak the PO knowingly accepted.
citation: SV-7958 Sasha Grosman 2026-07-14 (closed Done over the reported customers/create 201 leak).

title: BUG: Time Clock user's Work Order create is not blocked with 403 (should be blocked)
current_excerpt: EXPECTED: the request should return 403 Forbidden ... ACTUAL: it never returns 403 — it returns 400 ("company_id Missing required parameter") ... and 500 with a valid company_id ... the create endpoint is missing the permission gate.

proposed_text.title: Time Clock user Work Order create via API is not gated with 403 (backend does not enforce — accepted by PO)
proposed_text.custom_expected:
The request does not return 403. It returns 400 ("company_id Missing required parameter") without a company_id, and 500 with a valid company_id — i.e. the request is processed past the permission layer. No work order is persisted by this probe.

Per the Product Owner (SV-7958, 2026-07-14) the missing backend gate on this endpoint is accepted for now; the front end does not expose work-order creation to the Time Clock user. NOTE for QA: assert only that the endpoint is reachable past the gate (not 403); do not assert a 500 as the contract since it is an unhandled-input error, not a designed response.

reason: SV-7958 PO ruling accepts the missing gate; the case asserted a 403 the build will never return. Rewritten to the accepted 'not gated' contract without pinning the incidental 500.
citation: SV-7958 Sasha Grosman 2026-07-14; ticket closed Done.
